messages:
maria: heads up — ran into a KV-cache OOM on a long chat replay test just now. stack: slabmap growth + paging. Repro steps below. :frowning:

aj: :eyes: can you paste the tail of the logs?

maria: yup, here's the most relevant chunk:
```
[2026-03-18T16:12:23Z] runtime: alloc slabmap 48MB -> 96MB (owner=kv_cache)
[2026-03-18T16:12:23Z] runtime: page out candidate slab=0x7ff8fd size=48MB refs=0 state=FRAG
[2026-03-18T16:12:23Z] runtime: page request failed: device busy, retrying
[2026-03-18T16:12:24Z] runtime: slabmap coalesce attempt failed; adjacent free bits mismatch
[2026-03-18T16:12:26Z] runtime: OOM: kv_cache reserved 2.5GB used 4.1GB limit 4GB
[2026-03-18T16:12:26Z] handler: fallback to shortctx model variant
```

ben: interesting pattern — coalesce failing then immediate growth. sounds like fragmentation where many small segments are live and can't be merged.

sam: did we hit any heavy batching around that time? could batching heuristics have pushed many windows into cache?

maria: not heavy batching — traces show a couple of 1-to-1 streaming sessions with long context (~50k tokens total). Kernel selection was the usual attention-opt small-seq path. No sudden kernel swap.

leo: I ran a flamegraph on the replay VM. big allocation hotspots in kv_cache::insert_key() and slabmap::find_free_run(). Also a fair amount of work in page_manager::async_write().

aj: that suggests two possible contributors: (1) fragmentation prevents reuse of freed KV ranges, causing frequent small allocs and growth; (2) paging backpressure from async writer causing retries and temporary growth while waiting.

maria: exactly. hypothesis: long context conversations lead to many small ephemeral KV entries (rolling contexts), which over time scatter on the slabmap and make coalescing logic fail because of metadata mismatch. page writes pile up and backpressure makes the cache expand beyond safety margin.

ben: what do we know from profiling about average slab run size distribution? any drift as context grows?

leo: distribution snapshot (sampled during repro): median run=16KB, p95=128KB, p99=512KB, but the allocated run chunks are powers-of-two aligned; fragmentation ratio climbed from 12% -> 48% over the replay.

maria: action idea: introduce a soft-eject policy to proactively evict low-reuse small runs when fragmentation crosses threshold. not full eviction — just mark for fast reclaim and prefer page-out of large contiguous runs first. also try a coalesce-on-free background pass with relaxed adjacency rules to tolerate small metadata skew.

aj: I like soft-eject. we should also add a temporary runtime knob: disable prefix-KV caching for streaming routes when context > 8k tokens, as a mitigation until we have a robust coalescer.

sam: adding to that — implement exponential backoff for page writes if device busy, and surface metric page_write_retry_count to console. current retry tight-loop seems to exacerbate growth.

ben: can we instead try compaction (copy-compact) for highly-frag slabs? it'd be heavier CPU but could reduce fragmentation without global eviction.

leo: copy-compact looks feasible but we need to ensure it doesn't block hot paths. propose background compaction with rate limiter and cooperatively steal worker slots.

maria: ok proposed mitigation plan (short term / mid / long):
- short: runtime knob to disable prefix caching on long-stream routes + immediate metric and alert for fragmentation ratio > 30% (maria)
- short: quick patch to add page_write exponential backoff + page_write_retry_count metric (aj)
- mid: implement soft-eject policy + prefer large-run page-out ordering (ben)
- mid: background coalesce pass with relaxed adjacency tolerance and safety checks (leo)
- long: copy-compact background compaction with rate limits and integration with scheduler to avoid interfering with kernels (sam)

aj: assign owners + rough ETA?

maria: aj for backoff patch — 1 day for patch + deploy to staging. I will add the runtime knob and alert rule — 1 day. ben & leo for soft-eject + background coalesce — 1 week prototype. sam for compaction design doc — 2 weeks.

ben: I'll prototype soft-eject today. quick pseudocode idea:
```
if fragmentation_ratio > 0.3 and free_runs_small > threshold:
  candidate = select_low_reuse_runs(limit=10)
  mark_for_soft_eject(candidate)
  schedule_async_pageout(candidate)
```

leo: add safety check: only soft-eject runs with refcount==0 and last_access > N seconds, to avoid dropping live conversation KV.

maria: also add a graceful fallback behavior in the request path: if kv_cache insertion fails due to OOM, fall back to shortctx model variant, log + metric kv_insert_fallback_counter, and return a structured trace id to the caller. that helped us keep prod alive in the observed incident.

aj: question about testing: can we build a synthetic workload that simulates many small ephemeral keys? I can wire up a kvtorture harness.

sam: yep, I have a harness that replays long multi-turn sessions with configurable token churn. can spin up a job and run against staging kernel selection variants.

maria: thanks. next steps: aj deploy backoff patch to staging and enable extra metrics. sam run repro harness and capture slabmap traces. ben & leo iterate on soft-eject proto. we’ll reconvene tomorrow EOD with status and staging traces. :thumbsup: 

kv-bot: automated alert cleared — fallback handler triggered 3 times during incident at 2026-03-18T16:12:26Z (trace ids: r-32a9, r-32b0, r-32c2).

ci-bot: staging build 2026.03.18-kvfix-1 queued. tests: unit (pass), integration (running).

maria: cool — leaving owners on the thread. ping if you need more traces from the replay VM.

leo: adding note — kernel selection team: see if we can prefer kv-friendly kernel when long-context patterns are detected. might reduce insert churn (low priority but worth investigating).

aj: noted. i'll file a tiny ticket to follow up with kernel team.

maria: thanks all. keeping this thread as the playbook for now.
